intelligence.enrichment: Non-communicable diseases are usually linked to lifestyle, diet, and environment, and their control focuses on managing symptoms and improving quality of life through medication, lifestyle changes, rehabilitation, early diagnosis, and continuous care. Changes such as more processed food, less physical activity, and other lifestyle or environmental factors increase non-communicable disease risk; sustained care and lifestyle changes help control the disease. The learner correctly applies this rule: Non-communicable diseases are usually linked to lifestyle, diet, and environment, and their control focuses on managing symptoms and improving quality of life through medication, lifestyle changes, rehabilitation, early diagnosis, and continuous care. A disease becomes controllable when the sick person is kept away from others for a few days.
